No — the healthcheck in compose: 15s interval, 5 retries, start_period 300s. After the start_period (300s) and 5 failed checks, the service becomes "unhealthy", and compose's dependency check `service_healthy` fails, and... but compose with `up -d` doesn't kill already-started containers. However, the containers that were waiting (backend, worker, dashboard) failed to start: "Error dependency ml-service failed to start".

Wait, but ml-service is healthy now (Up 24 min, healthy). The health status flipped after the model was loaded. But the backend/worker/dashboard containers didn't start because the up command failed at an earlier point (around 300s+75s after start). Since `docker compose up -d` returned, those services were never started.

Hmm, actually, looking more carefully: the error "Error dependency ml-service failed to start" — compose was waiting for ml-service to become healthy. ml-service's healthcheck: start_period 300s, then retries 5 at 15s intervals = about 300s + 75s = around 375s until it becomes unhealthy. At that point compose gave up and marked the dependent containers as error.

But now ml-service is healthy. So I just need to run `docker compose up -d` again (without --build) to start the remaining services: migrate has already exited (0), and backend/worker/dashboard should now be able to start because the dependency is satisfied.
